::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 31st [1870]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library. Add MSS 54920: 244-5
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd)
Do you not think that the [parallel history](cmy_books/cmybook_89.qmd)[^1] should come out in time for Schools to set themselves up with this winter. The one I wrote it for is crying out for it, and it seems in vain to wait for a neater finish to France than the fall of the Empire.

I am glad you give hopes of clearing off the old [History of Christian Names](cmy_books/cmybook_48.qmd) I have them bristling with corrections, and I should begin by cutting out large pieces of the book - but alas, I have acquired no further knowledge of the Keltic names - always the weakest point in the book. Only I do know that some part is more desperately wrong than the rest.

I have been writing to [Miss Martin](people/person_971.qmd) about the [Founders and Pioneers](cmy_books/cmybook_90.qmd). I believe they are ready now.

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Her *A Parallel History of France and England, consisting of Outlines and Dates* (London: Macmillan 1871) was on the verge of publication.
